A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TH2T research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original TH2T experiments, including benchmark accuracy, response length, latency, component ablations, and difficulty and redundancy analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional comparisons, difficulty-assessment controls, and first-token confidence measurements. These qualify independently of the externally sourced AdaCtrl results.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same two-stage fine-tuning procedure: difficulty-prefix supervision using short/long reasoning data, followed by redundancy and looping hypnosis with truncation. The detection, completeness-checking, and inference procedures remain substantively unchanged; the prospective/retrospective terminology explains their existing roles.

E1.justification: Both train using GSM8K and MATH and evaluate on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME2024, OmniMath, and GPQA. The difficulty strata and application domains are retained. Additional comparator, ablation, and difficulty-assessment configurations concern existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 5 compares only the original Qwen models and TH2T on AIME2024, OmniMath, and GPQA. v3 Table 1 adds D-Prompt, NoThinking, TokenSkip, and CoT-Valve to those comparisons. It also adds externally sourced AdaCtrl-7B results on GSM8K, MATH-500, and AIME2024, substantially expanding comparator participation.

E3.justification: v3 adds a two-option difficulty-assessment control and a first-token confidence metric. Its appendix changes maximum generation length for OmniMath and GPQA from 8,192 to 16,384. Baseline evaluation is now described as reimplementation except for AdaCtrl, whereas v2 imports relative results for TokenSkip and CoT-Valve. These substantially revise the reported protocol without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds binary-option difficulty controls in Figure 2 and internal-confidence analysis in Table 2, and extends difficulty/redundancy component ablations to three additional retained benchmarks. It removes the starting-model ablation in v2 Table 4. The difficulty-level breakdown, training dynamics, response-length examples, and case studies are retained, with several relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 42 and greedy decoding, without introducing repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new first-token confidence measurements describe model outputs rather than statistical uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive OOD comparator and ablation results, AdaCtrl entries, binary difficulty-assessment outcomes, and confidence values. Some existing results are revised: TH2T-7B AIME2024 accuracy is approximately 46.7% in v2 Figure 5 and 50.0% in v3 Table 1. Detailed latency/speedup entries and the starting-model ablation results disappear. Shared GSM8K/MATH main-table scores and Llama results remain unchanged; revisions under changed generation limits do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The dataset definitions, reasoning-chunk formulation, and hypnosis/truncation equations retain their mathematical substance after renumbering and reindexing. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation appears. The expanded global/local account is conceptual motivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that two-stage self-hypnosis develops difficulty and redundancy cognition while reducing inference costs by over 70% on easy tasks and 40% on hard tasks with preserved performance. The prospective/retrospective framing elaborates these existing contributions without introducing a distinct core claim.

C2.justification: v3 interprets higher first-token confidence as evidence that enhanced cognition is represented internally and develops the global-strategy/local-execution explanation. It adds the limitation that discrete difficulty labels simplify a continuum and removes the starting-model failure discussion. The existing RL-cost and model-capability limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 8,000 final training examples while retaining the earlier 6,400-example Stage-1 description; this does not establish an increase in training data. Hardware changes from two to four 80GB H800 GPUs, and baseline provenance is revised. LoRA hyperparameters and appendix prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al.'s AdaCtrl and Fu et al.'s Deep Think with Confidence. It also introduces a more explicit critique of model-based methods as behaviorally rigid and contrasts them with TH2T's metacognitive intervention. The existing literature coverage and central novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, literature review, and methodological explanations are extensively rewritten around prospective and retrospective intervention. Literature categories and experimental analyses are reorganized, sections become numbered, appendices are reordered, and limitations move into the main document.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned around five benchmarks, replacing latency and gain columns with additional benchmark blocks. Figure 2 expands to four panels, Figure 4 is redrawn, and the difficulty-level plot moves from the appendix into the main text. Table removal, figure resizing, appendix redistribution, and the changed page format substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: The broader OOD comparisons and two-option difficulty controls strengthen empirical support, and the continuous-difficulty limitation improves qualification. However, v3 removes detailed latency evidence while retaining speedup claims and drops v2's informative starting-model failure ablation. Its new confidence analysis also supports strong mechanistic interpretations without clearly defining the confidence calculation. These material gains and losses leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
